mn-renters-credit.name: Minnesota Renter's Credit (Certificate of Rent Paid, Form M1, Schedule M1RENT)
mn-renters-credit.outcome: Refundable credit of up to $2,720 for tax year 2025 for household income below $77,570; landlords must give a Certificate of Rent Paid by January 31
mn-renters-credit.limits: One state; the amount shrinks as income rises, and the building's owner must have paid property tax. Other states have different or no renter credits.

pa-rent-rebate.name: Pennsylvania Property Tax/Rent Rebate program
pa-rent-rebate.outcome: Up to $1,000 for rent or property tax paid in 2025; income limit $48,110; for people 65 and older, widows and widowers 50 and older, and people with disabilities 18 and older; deadline December 31, 2026; apply free on myPATH
pa-rent-rebate.locator: "This year's income limit for rebate applicants is now $48,110."
pa-rent-rebate.limits: Department of Revenue press release. The $1,000 maximum is only for incomes of $8,550 or less; most eligible renters get $380 to $770. Limited to older people and people with disabilities.

united-way-211.name: United Way 211 housing expenses help
united-way-211.outcome: Dial 211 to reach someone who can find local options to pay rent, mortgage, or utility bills and connect you with your local housing authority
united-way-211.locator: "the best resource for help finding options to pay your rent"
united-way-211.limits: A referral line, not a fund; what's available depends on local programs and their money that month.

liheap.name: Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP), via USAGov
liheap.outcome: Helps pay heating or cooling bills and emergency services during an energy crisis; each state and territory sets its own income rules; some offices take online applications
liheap.locator: "help you pay heating or cooling bills"
liheap.limits: Federal page; rules for renters whose heat is included in rent vary by state, and funds can run out during the season.

avail-negotiation.name: Avail renter survey on negotiating at lease renewal (reported by CNBC via NBC Bay Area)
avail-negotiation.outcome: Only 28% of renters negotiated at their latest renewal; about 1 in 4 who tried got a lower price, up from 17% in October 2022; tips include offering a longer lease and pointing to on-time payments
avail-negotiation.locator: "from 17% in October 2022 to just over 25% as of April 2023"
avail-negotiation.limits: Secondary news story about a survey by Avail, a platform for small landlords; 2023 market conditions; not a random national sample.

zillow-concessions.name: Zillow April 2026 Rental Market Report on concessions (reported by Scotsman Guide)
zillow-concessions.place: United States; Denver, Charlotte, Dallas, Austin, Nashville
zillow-concessions.outcome: Nearly 40% of Zillow rental listings in April 2026 offered concessions such as a free month of rent, waived fees, or discounted move-in costs; Denver 68.3%, New York City 18.4%
zillow-concessions.locator: "a free month of rent, waived fees, and discounted move-in costs"
zillow-concessions.limits: Secondary trade story about Zillow's own report. Concessions are common where lots of apartments are being built and rare in tight markets like New York City or Buffalo.

fair-market-rent-map.name: Fair Market Rent Map (HUD Small Area Fair Market Rent data by ZIP code)
fair-market-rent-map.outcome: Free heat map and Small Area Fair Market Rents for every ZIP code from HUD data, by bedroom count
fair-market-rent-map.locator: "HUD Small Area Fair Market Rent (SAFMR) data for every ZIP code"
fair-market-rent-map.limits: Third-party site, not run by the Department of Housing and Urban Development; fair market rents are set for voucher programs and lag current listings.

ca-ab1482.name: California Tenant Protection Act (AB 1482), City of Alameda FAQ
ca-ab1482.outcome: Yearly increases capped at 5% plus local inflation, or 10%, whichever is lower; Alameda's cap is 6.3% for increases from August 1, 2025, through July 31, 2026; units are exempt for their first 15 years
ca-ab1482.limits: City FAQ; single-family homes owned by individuals are exempt if the tenant got written notice. The statewide law runs until 2030.

ca-ag-enforcement.name: California attorney general's first AB 1482 settlement (reported by the California Apartment Association)
ca-ag-enforcement.outcome: Settlement with a Silicon Valley property manager and developer accused of raising rents an average of 151%; more than $300,000 expected to be refunded to tenants
ca-ag-enforcement.locator: "This is a first for my office."
ca-ag-enforcement.limits: Landlord-association news post; the increases were allegations settled without trial.

wa-rent-cap.name: Washington statewide rent cap signed by Gov. Bob Ferguson (KUOW)
wa-rent-cap.outcome: Signed May 7, 2025: yearly increases capped at 7% plus inflation, or 10%, whichever is lower; new buildings exempt for 12 years; limits expire in 2040; manufactured home communities capped at 5%
wa-rent-cap.limits: Public radio story; landlords said they were exploring a legal challenge. Rent caps are contested among economists.

colorado-junk-fees.name: Colorado HB25-1090 price transparency and junk fees law (Colorado House Democrats)
colorado-junk-fees.outcome: Since January 1, 2026, advertised prices generally must show the total; the purpose of any fee outside the total must be disclosed; renters' fee increases capped at 2% a year. Sponsor Naquetta Ricks: junk fees often aren't disclosed until checkout
colorado-junk-fees.locator: "Junk fees are often not disclosed until a consumer is ready to check out."
colorado-junk-fees.limits: Press release from the bill's party caucus; it doesn't list exactly which fees are covered.

who-owns-what.name: Who Owns What, by JustFix.nyc (reported by 6sqft)
who-owns-what.outcome: Free tool that maps every building tied to a landlord from city registration data covering over 170,000 buildings, with code violations, evictions, and changes in rent-regulated units
who-owns-what.limits: Launch story from 2018; New York only, because it depends on the city's landlord registration data. The tool's own about page didn't load.

kc-independence-towers.name: Independence Towers Tenant Union and KC Tenants rent strike settlement
kc-independence-towers.outcome: After an 8-month rent strike that ended June 4, 2025, the new owner agreed to keep rents at what most tenants pay now for the first year, permanent heating and cooling (HVAC) repair by November 2025, a $75 monthly discount until then, and in-unit repairs by year-end
kc-independence-towers.limits: One building, terms as reported by local TV; rent strikes carry eviction risk and the union organized for months first.

nesterly.name: Nesterly intergenerational home sharing (NPR/WGBH via Public Radio East)
nesterly.outcome: A graduate student paid $650 a month, less than half the cost of a studio, for a room in a Boston brownstone, doing chores like taking out the trash and shoveling snow; Nesterly runs background checks and a payment system
nesterly.locator: "less than half the cost of a studio"
nesterly.limits: 2019 story; then only in Boston and nearby communities. Current coverage not checked.

minneapolis-zoning.name: Minneapolis zoning reforms and 2040 plan, Pew analysis (reported by NPR via WHYY)
minneapolis-zoning.outcome: From 2017 to 2022 Minneapolis grew its housing stock 12% while rents rose 1%; rents in the rest of Minnesota rose 14%
minneapolis-zoning.limits: Secondary story about Pew's analysis; shows a correlation, not proof the zoning changes caused the rent difference.

austin-rents.name: Austin building surge and falling rents, Pew study (reported by Governing)
austin-rents.outcome: Median rent fell from $1,546 at the end of 2021 to $1,296 at the start of 2026 per Pew; rents in large apartment buildings fell 7% in 2024; evictions still rose
austin-rents.limits: Secondary story; Pew's own page blocked the fetch. Evictions kept climbing even as rents fell.

sf-algorithm-ban.name: San Francisco ban on algorithmic rent-setting devices (Local News Matters)
sf-algorithm-ban.outcome: On September 3, 2024 the Board of Supervisors banned the sale or use of algorithmic devices to set rents or occupancy; civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; first city in America to pass such a law
sf-algorithm-ban.locator: "the first city in America to pass such a law"
sf-algorithm-ban.limits: Too new to show an effect on rents; the story doesn't report how many landlords used such software.

realpage-settlement.name: Justice Department proposed settlement with RealPage (Associated Press via News4JAX)
realpage-settlement.outcome: RealPage can no longer use real-time nonpublic data; training data must be at least one year old. Greystar, the nation's largest landlord, agreed to pay $50 million in a class action and $7 million to nine states. Philadelphia and Seattle passed ordinances against the practice
realpage-settlement.locator: "must be at least one year old"
realpage-settlement.limits: Wire story from November 2025; the settlement needed a judge's approval, and RealPage admitted no wrongdoing.

montgomery-hpf.name: Housing Opportunities Commission of Montgomery County Housing Production Fund
montgomery-hpf.outcome: $100 million revolving construction fund set up in 2021 to produce 6,000 new homes; at least 30% of units income-restricted; first project The Laureate, 268 units at Shady Grove Metro
montgomery-hpf.limits: The agency's own page; the 6,000-home goal is a target, and only one building was finished at the time.

vienna-social-housing.name: Vienna social housing (Climate and Community Institute)
vienna-social-housing.outcome: Over 40% of the city's housing, about 400,000 units, is social housing; limited-profit rents are 23% lower on average than private market rents
vienna-social-housing.locator: "The majority of Vienna's renters live in the city's 400,000 units"
vienna-social-housing.limits: Advocacy research group; Vienna built this over a century, with national housing funds US cities don't have.

nyc-right-to-counsel.name: New York City right to counsel for tenants, first-year report (Next City)
nyc-right-to-counsel.outcome: Under the 2017 law, in fiscal 2018 21,955 residents in 7,847 households kept their homes after getting lawyers paid by the city's Office of Civil Justice
nyc-right-to-counsel.limits: Program outcome numbers, not a controlled comparison; rollout was ZIP code by ZIP code.

jchs-cost-burden.name: Harvard Joint Center for Housing Studies, State of the Nation's Housing 2025 (summarized by the National Low Income Housing Coalition)
jchs-cost-burden.outcome: A record 22.6 million renter households, half of all renters, spent 30% or more of income on housing and utilities in 2023; cost-burdened renters earning under $30,000 had about $250 a month left
jchs-cost-burden.locator: "just $250 remaining to cover all other basic needs"
jchs-cost-burden.limits: Advocacy group's summary; the Joint Center's own release blocked the fetch.
